key_insight: A general-relativistic superfluid framework establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity, enabling simulations of neutron-star vortex dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stable computational studies of superfluid dynamics relevant to pulsar glitches and neutron-star tidal interactions.
method: Include entrainment, vortex forces, and vortex line energy in relativistic two-fluid hydrodynamics.
Express vortex dynamics through effective electric and magnetic fields using an analogy with force-free electrodynamics.
Combine finite-volume evolution with constrained transport of superfluid vorticity and implicit electric-field evolution.
evidence_signal: Validation includes an exact relativistic superfluid Riemann solution, Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, and oscillation modes of global relativistic two-fluid neutron-star equilibria.
watch_item: The spin-down demonstration prescribes vortex release and repinning, so its residual differential rotation and vortex twist require testing with more realistic unpinning physics.
paper_title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
